$comment: Trigger patterns for the pre-publication credential scan.
This file is data, not code: you can tighten or extend detection over time
without touching the module. Point `secret_patterns_file` in your config at
your own copy to override these defaults entirely, or add to them with
`secret_scan_extra_patterns`.
Each entry:
name      - label shown in the abort message (the matched value never is)
regex     - Python re syntax, matched against text column content
prefilter - optional literal used as a cheap SQL LIKE pre-filter so large
snapshots stay fast. It MUST be a substring that every value
matching `regex` contains, otherwise findings are missed.
Omit it when no such literal exists - the scanner then reads
the full column for that pattern (correct, but slower).
Deliberately NOT included: generic rules like 'long hexadecimal string'.
They match checksums, UUIDs and git SHAs, which are legitimate database
content. A scanner that cries wolf gets switched off, and a switched-off
scanner protects nothing. Prefer a precise pattern per vendor.
Every vendor prefix is anchored with `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])`. A credential prefix
starts a token; it never continues a word. Without the anchor `sk-` matches
inside ordinary text - 'task-scheduler', 'ask-2026', 'risk-and-reward' - and
because the scan is fail-closed, those false hits block publication entirely.
Measured on a real 53 MB knowledge database: 33 hits, all of them words.
